The region growing code uses a stack, adds a pixel when abs(intensity - seed intensity) < threshold (threshold = 50) and pushes its 4 neighbors.
Region growing is effective for segmenting regions with uniform characteristics.
Clustering-based segmentation groups pixels into clusters by feature similarity using K-Means, Mean-Shift or DBSCAN.
Clustering techniques like K-Means or Mean-Shift group similar pixels by feature similarity such as color values.
The global threshold example is cv2.threshold(image, 128, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY).
In region growing, a pixel whose intensity difference from the seed is below the threshold is added to the segmented region (mask set to 255) and its neighbours are pushed on the stack.
K-means initialization chooses the number of clusters K and initializes K centroids randomly or by a heuristic.
Semantic segmentation gives every pixel of the same class the same label; instance segmentation also separates different instances (objects) of the same class.
Deep learning-based segmentation uses CNNs for semantic and instance segmentation; suitable for complex tasks and large datasets.
Panoptic segmentation combines semantic labels for stuff with instance labels for things.
Thresholding is typically performed on single-channel grayscale images.
LBP operates on grayscale images and defines a circular neighborhood around each pixel.
Segmentation divides an image into meaningful segments or regions, often separating objects from the background.
K-means features per pixel are RGB values or LAB/HSV for color images, or intensity for grayscale images.
Object recognition assigns a label to an object based on its descriptors.
Before plotting with Matplotlib, convert OpenCV's default BGR (Blue, Green, Red) to RGB with cv2.cvtColor(image, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB).
Matplotlib expects images in RGB order, while OpenCV stores colour images in BGR order.
cv2.cvtColor(src, code) converts colour spaces; cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB converts OpenCV BGR to RGB for Matplotlib, COLOR_BGR2HSV converts to HSV and COLOR_BGR2GRAY to grayscale.
plt.imshow needs cmap='gray' to display a grayscale image without false colors; plt.axis('off') hides the axes.
Visual characteristics used to group pixels in segmentation are color, texture and intensity; file size and metadata are not visual characteristics.
cv2.imshow displays an image in a window and cv2.waitKey(0) waits for a key press before closing it.
Affine transformations always preserve parallelism; projective transformations do not.
cv2.cvtColor(image, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY) converts a color image to grayscale.
SIFT step 1, scale-space extrema detection, finds keypoint candidates at multiple scales using a Difference of Gaussians (DoG).
The integer value of cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB (color conversion code) is 4.
The integer value of cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY (color conversion code) is 6.
LoG stands for Laplacian of Gaussian; it combines Gaussian smoothing and Laplacian edge detection and highlights zero-crossings of the second derivative.
The integer value of cv2.COLOR_BGRA2BGR (color conversion code) is 1.
The Difference of Gaussians (DoG) subtracts two Gaussian-blurred versions of the image: DoG = L(x, y, k sigma) - L(x, y, sigma).
The integer value of cv2.COLOR_BGR2HSV (color conversion code) is 40.
The integer value of cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR (color conversion code) is 4.
